newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA SAYS BAND ABANDONED BECAUSE OF REGION.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA SAYS BAND ABANDONED BECAUSE OF REGION.

text.p: Indonesian central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Thursday that the bank's decision to abandon its intervention band was taken because other countries in the region had floated their currencies.

He told a capital markets conference that the Thai baht and the Philippine peso had been recently floated whereas the Singapore dollar and the Malaysian ringgit were also traded without pre-announced limits.
"Indonesia is the only with a band," Djiwandono said. "It's no longer an advantage."
"That's why we are abandoning the band. We didn't do this from weakness," he added. "Our system has been very consistent in moving bit by bit in the end to really float it (the rupiah)".
Djiwandono also said the central bank had intervened in the forward dollar market with $500 million on Wednesday to prop up the rupiah.

The unit, which has been weak because of a contagion effect from the malaise in regional currencies for several weeks, plunged to a low of 2,682 against the dollar on Wednesday before the intervention.
It plunged again on Thursday after the central bank scrapped the band, and was trading at 2,780/90 against the dollar at 0510 GMT.
